limits: The nine projection/route tests and six decision-order tests are local synthetic tests. Native Forgejo tree/participant semantics are separately bound to bootstrap VM005, which did not execute this complete permanent service.
Native qualification links the earlier local qualification002; this receipt explicitly binds the corrected source set003 and the same unchanged native semantics.
No credential reader, branch-protection observer, permanent merge privilege, signed delivery decision, service or activation is supplied by these components.

The manifest remains opaque at this layer: the future loader must validate its schema and compare every consumed artifact/source against the signed validation attestation before any merge/delivery decision.

API observations are non-atomic. Postmerge recheck is limited to expected main/merge and unchanged chosen approval; full protection, other reviews, deployment state and artifact checks remain separate obligations.
The dismissed-approval eligibility rule is deliberately stricter than native max(non-dismissed id); native rejection blocking still follows active decisions.
No tests were rerun and no production request, credential or human review was created by this review.
reviewed_properties: Tree OID comes from the fixed encoded head^{tree} route, not Forgejo commit.tree.sha; response URLs and partial tree entries are never used as authority or inventory.
GET transport changes only the new fixed tree route and review-contract import; dedicated socket watchdog and response limits remain byte-exact.
Complete review pages are matched to native active participant IDs before pending requests are projected. Team or missing commit-ID shapes remain refused.

Decision order is max(id), independent of edit timestamp. A separate active non-dismissed map blocks unresolved rejections/requests; the latest overall map conservatively prevents resurrecting a dismissed approval.
The independently reproduced other-reviewer rejection masked by a newer dismissed approval is addressed by the active-map check; six targeted signature tests cover this and related order cases.

Premerge recheck retains full collection/signature/binding and individual chosen-review reread. Postmerge now expects the chosen approver in the native participant list and still rereads that approval; it does not claim to recheck all other reviewers.
scope: independent review of permanent read-only projection and unsigned review binding corrections, with separate native semantic evidence
